Form 990 Schedule I as an alias source for the BMF

Source: R/schedi.R
pf_schedi.Rd

Schedule I Part II is where a non-PF 990 filer lists every grant it made to a US organization or government: recipient name, address, and EIN. That is the same speech act as 990-PF Part XIV — a grantmaker writing down who it paid — so the name representations come from the same distribution as the queries we are trying to match. The BMF gives one legal name per EIN; this gives many observed names.

Why it earns its place

Measured on the 50k benchmark (dev/SCHEDI-ALIAS-FINDINGS.md):

  • 95.6% agreement with the accepted EIN on grants the cascade already resolved confidently — and the error rate is a clean function of n_filers, the number of distinct grantmakers who wrote that spelling: 86.1% at one filer, 95.4% at 2-4, 98.0% at 5-19, 99.0% at 20+.

  • 18.1% of the NO tier gets a hit; roughly half of those are both BMF-present and multi-filer, worth about +2.2 points.

  • It resolves rebrands (Lakeview Pantry -> Nourishing Hope), mergers (Foundation for National Progress -> Center for Investigative Reporting), and brand-vs-legal names (USA FOR UNHCR, VOTEORG) — none of which any string metric can reach.

The trap this design avoids

Do not use the alias to assign an EIN, and do not block on it. If the alias merely surfaces the BMF row for Nourishing Hope as a candidate for the query Lakeview Pantry, the comparison step scores those two names against each other, gets ~0, and the veto layer discards the correct answer. The match is justified by the alias observation, not by name similarity. So the alias name is written into the reference as a row in its own right, and the existing exact-name pass resolves it with no new comparison logic.
